Resolves #21812

The Board inline-title test allows less than a quarter of a CSS pixel between the before and editing measurements. That covers the observed 0.09375 px difference. The 4.8 px growth recorded in #21712 still fails, and the rename, Escape and focus checks stay in the same spec.

Evidence: L2 (exact hosted failure, matcher controls and local headless E2E) → L2 required (geometry regression and hosted rerun).

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 subpixel allowance with a hard limit | The Playwright matcher accepts the observed 0.09375 px delta and rejects 0.25 px and the historical 4.8 px growth. |
| AC-2 hosted CardEditor case | CI-covered in `test/playwright/e2e/board/CardEditor.spec.mjs`. |

None.

The named CardEditor case passed three local headless Chrome runs with the change and again on the rebased commit. The previous precision-based matcher failed twice on the exact hosted pair. # PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical. This is a test-only tolerance change on one assertion, with no app, CSS or engine change.

**Verdict:** Approved

**Glance:**
- **The change.** At head `d8d24613b2`, the CardEditor test compares the card's height before and during the inline edit with `Math.abs(edited - before) < 0.25`. The old check was `toBeCloseTo(before, 1)`, which accepts less than 0.05 px.
- **Why it is safe.** #21812 measured the hosted drift at 0.09375 px (91.109375 → 91.203125). The regression this check guards is #21712's growth from 91.1 to 95.9 px. 0.25 px sits between those two numbers, so the test still fails on any real reflow and tolerates line-box rounding.
- **What I looked for.** I checked whether the widening hides a reflow the example could still produce, and found none: a wrapped or resized title moves the card by whole pixels. The rename, Escape and focus checks are untouched.
- **CI.** 29 checks pass at the head.

**Findings:** None.
